paths.description: Homepage and only discovered same-host content template; evaluated at desktop/mobile, preference, no-JS, network, performance, accessibility, security, and memory conditions.
Representative unknown same-host URL to evaluate HTTP/network failure recovery.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is byte-identical to the default screenshot (101,328 bytes), and the DOM probe reports color-scheme: normal with a fixed white content surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface, text, link, and background colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is deliberately removed and mobile links have very small targets.
findings.evidence: The authored reset contains :focus { outline: 0 } and a:hover/a:active { outline:none}; the active-link probe found outline-style none and visible policy links only 15px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove blanket outline suppression, add a strong :focus-visible style, and enlarge link hit areas to at least 24 CSS px (preferably 44px for primary touch actions).

findings.summary: The error path offers no recovery or site context.
findings.evidence: A representative unknown URL returns a bare “Not Found / The resource could not be found” page with no link home, contact route, or retry guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded 404 with a concise explanation, a link back to the disclaimer page, and the support contact.

findings.summary: Lab LCP is just outside the good Core Web Vitals threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 2.7s (good threshold 2.5s), although the direct trace measured 1.11s; CLS was 0 and TBT was 0ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the first paint by reducing the document/font critical path and keeping nonessential analytics out of the initial load.

findings.summary: Render-blocking styles and third-party dependencies dominate a very small page.
findings.evidence: HAR identifies three parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets, including Google Fonts; 15 of 22 requests and 125,649 of 143,661 transferred bytes are third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Self-host/subset the font, consolidate critical CSS, and defer or remove nonessential analytics until an appropriate consent/interaction point.

findings.summary: Unused analytics JavaScript dominates shipped script bytes.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed unused-javascript; HAR shows Yandex Metrika tag.js at 89,997 bytes, accounting for nearly all of 91,923 transferred script bytes on a static disclaimer.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove session analytics that does not provide proportionate value, or load a minimal analytics path after consent and idle time.

findings.summary: Most secondary copy fails WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse/axe measured #7d7d7d text on white at 4.11:1 for 12px normal-weight paragraphs and links, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken secondary text and links to achieve at least 4.5:1, then verify all states with an automated contrast audit.

findings.summary: The document has no headings and keyboard focus is invisible.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found zero h1–h6 elements and only a main landmark; focus probing found outline:none on every visible link.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one descriptive h1 and logical h2 sections, add semantic header/footer/nav where appropriate, and restore visible focus indicators.

findings.summary: A tracking image lacks an accessible alternative and the logo is exposed as empty.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-alt for the injected 1×1 rtmark image; the image probe found both rendered images without a non-null alt value.
findings.suggestedFix: Give decorative/tracking images alt="" (and role=presentation where useful); give the logo meaningful alt text only if it conveys identity not already present as text.

findings.summary: Dense 12px secondary copy is hard to read, especially on mobile.
findings.evidence: Computed CSS sets the long secondary paragraphs to 12px with 4.11:1 contrast; the mobile screenshot shows long dense blocks with cramped line spacing.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase body copy size/line-height, constrain readable line length, and pair the typography change with the contrast correction.

findings.summary: A missing favicon generates a console/network error.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console reports https://tukrd.com/favicon.ico returning 404; the HAR also records that 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an explicit favicon resource and link element, or ensure /favicon.ico returns a valid icon.

findings.summary: Images do not reserve their intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports missing width and height on both images. CLS happened to remain 0 in this run, but the document does not reserve dimensions declaratively.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width and height attributes matching each intrinsic aspect ratio; keep CSS max-width:100%;height:auto.

findings.summary: Chrome reports unresolved inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed inspector-issues (alongside a third-party-cookie warning, judged separately under privacy).
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the specific DevTools Issues entries, then rerun Lighthouse; avoid introducing deprecated or blocked browser behaviour.

findings.summary: Search metadata does not describe the page.
findings.evidence: The title is only “Surveza” and no meta description exists; Lighthouse failed meta-description.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a specific title such as “tukrd.com survey hosting notice | Surveza” and add a concise description matching the visible disclaimer.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are absent.
findings.evidence: No canonical link or hreflang is present; /sitemap.xml returns a Not Found HTML response. robots.txt itself is valid and permits search.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a self-referencing canonical and publish a valid sitemap (or intentionally document why this single URL does not need one).

findings.summary: The public organization notice has no share-preview or structured metadata.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter metadata and minimal Organization/WebPage JSON-LD that matches the visible content.

findings.summary: Core security headers are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirms HTTPS but no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, nosniff, a restrictive CSP (including frame-ancestors), and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; retain the existing strict-origin referrer policy.

findings.summary: A static disclaimer starts session analytics and cookie syncing without visible choice.
findings.evidence: Trackers probe records five third-party origins; DOM initializes Yandex Metrika with webvisor:true, while HAR records 15 third-party requests and cookie-sync redirects. Four Yandex cookies use SameSite=None, including two lasting 365 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove Webvisor/cookie syncing unless demonstrably necessary; otherwise gate nonessential analytics behind informed consent, minimise retention, and batch sparse events.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: No HSTS, frame protection, Permissions-Policy, or CSP/Trusted Types policy is present; Lighthouse also reports third-party-cookie and inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS and frame-ancestors, deny unused permissions, set a restrictive CSP, and remove third-party cookie dependencies.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling is an unstyled dead end.
findings.evidence: The 404 route is a bare server response with no branding, navigation, home link, or support contact.
findings.suggestedFix: Install a custom 404/error document that preserves site identity and gives recovery actions.

findings.summary: Background analytics and cookie-sync work is disproportionate to the page.
findings.evidence: A static notice causes 15 third-party requests, multiple tracking pixel redirects, and Webvisor full-session analytics.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove full-session analytics; if measurement remains necessary, collect only explicit, low-volume events and batch/defer them.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes 87% of transferred bytes without visible user value.
findings.evidence: HAR records 125,649 third-party bytes out of 143,661 total; Yandex tag.js alone is 89,997 bytes and Google Fonts adds 27,892 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party budget, remove Yandex/session replay, and self-host/subset the single font or use a system stack.
